Fit a Structural Equation Model by Maximum Likelihood

Source: R/fit-sem.R
fit_sem.Rd

Fits a model written in lavaan-style syntax to raw data with medfit's native maximum-likelihood engine, and returns a SEMFit object. The engine handles observed and latent variables, user labels, fixed values, starts and bounds, equality and inequality constraints (==, <, >, linear or nonlinear), and defined parameters (:=) with delta-method standard errors.

Usage

fit_sem(
  model,
  data,
  information = c("observed", "expected"),
  n_starts = NULL,
  control = list(),
  weights = NULL,
  se_type = c("model", "sandwich"),
  meanstructure = TRUE,
  fixed_x = TRUE,
  sampling_weights = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  missing = c("listwise", "fiml")
)

Arguments

model

Character: model syntax. Lines may use ~ (regression), =~ (latent variable), ~~ (variance or covariance), label*variable modifiers, start(), lower() and upper(), and the constraint operators ==, <, > and :=. An intercept is written y ~ 1 (alone or with other terms, as in y ~ 1 + x) and turns on the mean structure. A product of two observed variables is written x:m on the right side of a regression (canonical name m:x); ?"medfit-syntax" lists the supported class and each limit.

data

A data frame with the model's observed variables. Numeric columns are used as is; a factor, character or logical column named on a regression's right side is expanded to 0/1 dummies (?"medfit-syntax" lists the rules and limits). Rows with missing values in those columns are dropped once (listwise deletion) and counted in n_dropped under the default missing = "listwise". Bounded missing = "fiml" accepts numeric model columns only, retains rows with any observed model variable, and drops only all-empty model rows; extra columns do not select rows.

information

Character: "observed" (default) or "expected" information for the standard errors. "expected" is an error for a model with a product term that has an endogenous factor (the product is a function of another variable, so the expected information gives wrong standard errors); use the default with se_type = "sandwich". Bounded FIML supports only "observed".

n_starts

Positive integer or NULL: number of optimizer starts tried before the fit is declared failed (NULL uses 5). Retries use perturbed starts drawn under a fixed seed and never change the caller's random number stream; with 3 or more starts the last attempt is the model's own moment-based start, so a start in a bad basin does not end the fit. With a nonlinear constraint, which can leave several local optima, every start is tried and the best accepted one is kept (a warning says when the accepted starts disagree); otherwise the first accepted start is used. A supported nonzero-product equality searches both sign branches independently, with n_starts starts per nonempty branch; aggregate diagnostics report the actual attempts, not the number of branches. For FIML, only NULL or 3 is supported: three starts per solver, with refinements counted separately.

control

List: options passed to the optimizer (nloptr). FIML requires the empty list under its initial validated numerical protocol.

weights

Optional numeric vector of non-negative case weights, one per row of data (NULL, the default, fits unweighted). The fit is weighted maximum likelihood on the weighted mean and covariance; the scale of the weights does not matter. Rows dropped for missing values drop their weights with them. Use with se_type = "sandwich". FIML rejects every non-NULL weight vector.

se_type

Character: "model" (default) takes the covariance of the estimates from the inverse information; "sandwich" uses the robust sandwich covariance \(A^{-1} B A^{-1}\) with casewise scores (HC0-type: it equals sandwich::vcovHC(type = "HC0") per equation and lavaan's robust standard errors with sampling.weights, and is smaller than the HC3 default of the glm route by a factor that shrinks like \(1/n\)). Model-based standard errors are not valid under weights.

meanstructure

Logical or NULL. TRUE (default) fits a mean structure; NULL fits one only when the model writes an intercept (y ~ 1, free or fixed); FALSE fits covariances only and errors if an intercept is written. With a mean structure every observed variable whose intercept is not written has a free one, so a model with only free intercepts has the same estimates and standard errors as the covariance-only fit. A latent variable's mean is fixed at 0. A model with a product term (y ~ x + m + x:m) always fits the mean structure (it needs the mediator intercept for the four-way decomposition), so with a product meanstructure = FALSE is an error. An explicit NULL or FALSE is kept as given for listwise fits. FIML requires TRUE.

fixed_x

TRUE (default), FALSE, or a character vector of exogenous observed variable names. The selected variables (TRUE: every exogenous observed variable, product columns included) have their mean (with a mean structure), variance and the exogenous covariances the model contains fixed at the sample moments of the estimation sample (weighted when weights are given) and removed from estimation, as lavaan does with fixed.x = TRUE. The structural estimates, their standard errors, the degrees of freedom and the chi-square do not change; the parameter count and the log likelihood do: the log likelihood (and so AIC and BIC) is conditional on the fixed variables, and glance()$fixed_x lists them. Models whose fixed_x sets or data differ cannot be compared with stats::anova(), mbco_sem(), AIC() or BIC(). A (co)variance or intercept statement on a selected variable is an error (lavaan would silently keep it free). The fixed rows stay in the parameter table (fixed_x column, no standard error) but not in coef() or vcov(). Left unset it resolves to an explicit subset: every exogenous observed variable (product and factor-dummy columns included) except those a ~~ or ~1 statement names, which are left free with a message of class medfit_message_fixed_x_lenient (an explicit TRUE errors there instead; an explicit FALSE is kept). glance()$fixed_x names the set the fit used.

sampling_weights

Renamed weights, the name fit_mediation() uses; the old name still works with a warning.

missing

Exact missing-data method: listwise (default) or bounded Gaussian fiml (no abbreviations). FIML requires explicit fixed_x = FALSE; see the Bounded FIML section. The argument is appended to preserve existing positional calls.

Value

A SEMFit object. With a product term whose factor is a regression target (x:m with m regressed on x), glance() reports the chi-square, df and p-value as NA with a note, and anova() and mbco_sem() refuse; see SEMFit-methods. diagnostics$ledger holds the versioned outcome ledger described below.

Defaults changed in 0.15.0

fixed_x is the exogenous observed variables (lavaan's fixed.x = TRUE) and meanstructure = TRUE, so a default fit matches a default lavaan::sem() fit. Against 0.14.x the parameter count, logLik(), AIC(), BIC() and the names in coef(), vcov() and tidy() change; the structural estimates and their standard errors did not change on the cases measured. Which random start a multi-start fit tries can change too (the retry seed follows the parameter names). To keep the 0.14.x results, pass fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL. The 0.14.x options(medfit.native_defaults) opt-in no longer has any effect.

Bounded FIML

Explicit missing = "fiml" fits a joint Gaussian random-X model under ignorable missingness (for example, MAR with the usual ignorability conditions). It evaluates observed components, without imputing values. It supports exactly three numeric continuous observed variables in X -> M -> Y, with the X -> Y path free or fixed exactly at zero, independent disturbances and free intercepts. Names and labels are arbitrary. Extra predictors, latent variables, products, factors, correlated disturbances, parameter ties, bounds, general constraints, defined parameters and syntax-supplied starts are not supported. Input checks and local numerical gates do not establish global identification, a global optimum or inference coverage.

Supply fixed_x = FALSE explicitly; omission, TRUE and named subsets are errors. Require meanstructure = TRUE, information = "observed", se_type = "model", no weights, empty control, and n_starts = NULL or 3. These numerical-control restrictions reproduce the initial validated protocol. Missing values never select FIML automatically, and a failed fit never falls back to listwise deletion. Native fit_mediation() forwards these settings through engine_args; its se_type = "model" remains a top-level argument.

nobs() counts rows with any observed model variable; n_dropped counts only all-empty rows. Singleton patterns and data with no complete rows are supported when the local identification and information checks pass. Original positional row IDs and pattern counts are retained. logLik() includes the full Gaussian constants, with its df attribute equal to the free-parameter count (8 or 9). AIC and BIC use that likelihood and retained row count. The discrepancy f and model-test df are NA: no saturated missing-data reference model is fitted.

Supported operations include SEMFit coefficient/covariance and likelihood summaries, parameter tidy/normal confidence intervals, and extraction followed by paths(), nie(), nde(), te(), coef(), vcov(), print/summary, tidy and normal path/effect confidence intervals. Extracted aliases follow topology; source labels/full covariance remain in the validated durable fit context. At a = b = 0, the NIE point value remains available but its inferential fields are unavailable; a known fixed direct path is a different case.

SEMFit glance() reports likelihood/IC fields with unavailable model-test fields; extracted-object glance(), quick(), pm(), bootstrap, profiles, MBCO and fit tests are deferred and refuse FIML objects. Object-aware package guards precede package-controlled refits/RNG/workers; opaque user callbacks and external-first dispatch remain outside that guarantee. Adapter/topology/numerical failures retain stage, reason, original parent and completed attempts; basic argument-type errors can occur earlier. A dedicated fiml-1 ledger binds likelihood, rows, settings and attempts; the version-1 ledger below continues to describe listwise fits. See the Methods and Formulas article, Bounded FIML, for the likelihood and the native engine guide for the supported workflow. Bounded FIML was introduced in 0.16.0; released 0.15.0 does not provide this option.

Nonzero-product search coverage

One equality c*a*b == q is supported when the constants and q/c are finite and nonzero, a and b are distinct free scalar labels after expanding definitions, and no other constraint row involves either label. The engine fits both signs of a independently with the existing optimizer and acceptance gates, respecting user bounds and effective variance floors. It returns the lowest accepted discrepancy only when each required sign branch is accepted or excluded by an explicit bounds contradiction. An unresolved branch stops the fit with medfit_error_no_convergence; an all-empty search returns no fit. Zero-product fitting is unchanged. Repeated factors, multiple product equalities, coupled rows and other unsupported shapes retain local search.

internals$search_evidence is a separate versioned internal record, not a change to the outcome-ledger schema. Its coverage is charted for covered sign branches, local for unsupported shapes, or unresolved for an incomplete search. It retains restrictions, context, branch states, candidates, objectives, gates and attempts; validation checks their attribution to the model and sample. Charted coverage does not prove a global optimum within a branch. Existing optimum status meanings are retained, and objects without this optional record remain usable. Counts distinguish optimizer starts, accepted starts and synthetic reference attempts.

The stored raw constraint residual is diagnostic only. Its optional standardized value uses the gradient and covariance at an already available matching reference fit without the tested restriction, never the projected constrained covariance. No additional fit or covariance calculation is requested. The ordinary optimizer reference lacks covariance, so the standard error and standardized residual are NA with reason reference_covariance_unavailable. These diagnostics do not affect acceptance or inference.

Constrained standard errors

Observed-information covariance includes the curvature of active nonlinear constraints; expected information retains its Fisher definition. Sandwich standard errors use the corresponding information as bread. Active inequalities, user bounds and solver variance floors give a local tangent covariance, with exactly zero variance for a pinned coordinate. This is not the full sampling distribution at a boundary. See the Methods and Formulas article, under Constraints, for the covariance formula.

Outcome ledger

diagnostics$ledger is a list with schema_version = 1L. Each node has id, parent_id, the exact parsed constraints, and context (the estimation sample, the model syntax and parameters, the likelihood domain, the settings and n_obs). enumeration records state and the number of required children; complete means every required restriction was attempted, not that any was globally optimized. outcome is resolved or unresolved. Separate fields record optimizer (acceptance state, original status, decrement, retries and optimum diagnostics), likelihood (availability and f), feasibility (witness or unknown), covariance (available, unavailable, not_retained or failed), improper, the retained notices (warnings and messages), the original condition (class, message, call) and the recursive children. IDs are deterministic positions within the call, not certificates of equivalent parameter spaces. No global optimum is asserted, and a failed branch is unknown, never certified infeasible.

A node whose constraints hold zero-product rows also has branch_map: state, raw_count, the parser factor_counts, unique_count and raw_to_canonical, a structural restriction-set ID for each raw row. The IDs collapse duplicate or permuted constraint rows, not arbitrary affine equivalence, and every raw row is still fitted in its original order (ties go to the first). More than 64 raw combinations, duplicates included, is refused before the grid is allocated, even when the unique count would be smaller; that node is not_enumerated, with an unknown unique count and no raw mapping, and nothing is fitted or certified. Its message prints the count without scientific notation, labels a count above \(2^{53}\) as approximate (a double need not be an exact cardinality there) and names an overflow; raw_count is Inf on overflow. If the map cannot be built while an error is recorded, its state is unavailable with that condition, and the original error is not replaced. The map is rebuilt from the node's constraints during validation, so a forged map is refused.

The one proof of emptiness in this version-1 ledger is the literal certificate literal_zero_nonzero: an explicit label == 0 equality and an explicit finite nonzero literal equality on the same parsed label (a == 0 with a == 1). Its label, source rows and values are kept in certificate and rebuilt from the node's own parsed parameters and constraints before any inference uses it. A certified-empty branch is retained with outcome = "excluded", feasibility = "certified_empty" and an unavailable likelihood: it is not fitted and is not a successful fit. No tolerance, solver status, numerical rank, bound, general affine contradiction or fixed value in the parameter table is a proof, and a literal too small to represent (1e-999) is unknown.

A zero-product fit returns only if at least one required branch resolves and every other branch resolves or is certified empty. A direct fit whose own equalities contradict literally stops with medfit_sem_infeasible, and a union whose every branch is certified empty with medfit_sem_empty_union; both are refinements of medfit_error_no_convergence and carry the ledger. Otherwise it stops with a medfit_error_no_convergence error, never a fit; the error carries the ledger of every required branch as $ledger and, when a branch survived, $best_survivor (its id and discrepancy f, diagnostic only, never a p-value). The union's own node does not aggregate its children's notices; inspect each child. The notices of a failed call are in the ledger only; the error message keeps its text. A data or model error keeps its own class and also carries $ledger. The estimation sample is stored once, on the root node; a descendant fitted on the same rows carries only context$sample_hash. A fit made before the ledger existed must be refitted before mbco_sem() can use it, which refuses it with a medfit_error_ledger error.

When the optimizer accepts a fit and the covariance stage explicitly diagnoses non-positive-definite information or a negative variance, the call stops with medfit_sem_covariance_error, never a fit. The class is a sibling of medfit_error_no_convergence: no optimizer failed, so the handlers that report an unresolved result for an optimizer failure do not take it. Its fields are schema_version = 1L, stage = "covariance", partial (the accepted optimizer result: f, theta, sample, domain, dimensions and settings; no vcov or defined) and ledger (the same node as partial$ledger, with covariance = "failed" and post_fit: versioned evidence with the original condition's class, message, call and diagnostic kind, information_not_pd or negative_variance). Other covariance errors propagate unchanged, without a retained likelihood. Singular information still warns and returns an NA covariance, recorded as unavailable rather than failed. The message is the original one. Resolved here means an accounted-for accepted likelihood, not a successful covariance. A union root reports the first failing branch's post_fit, in branch order, even when another branch supplies its minimum likelihood, and does not claim the winning branch failed: inspect the branch IDs. A branch that did not converge still stops the call with medfit_error_no_convergence first. Definition values and gradients are checked before the covariance, and model, data, optimizer, objective and other errors get no covariance certificate. The condition is not accepted as an input to mbco_sem(), and a fit that carries post_fit is refused with medfit_error_ledger.

See also

SEMFit, fit_mediation()

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + treatment\nab := a*b",
  data = mediation_demo, fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL
)
fit@defined
#>   name expr       est         se
#> 1   ab  a*b 0.3253207 0.08016376

# A treatment-by-mediator product: the four-way decomposition
fit4 <- fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ treatment\noutcome_int ~ treatment + mediator1 + treatment:mediator1",
  data = mediation_demo, se_type = "sandwich"
)
#> Warning: the model test is not valid for this model: the product 'mediator1:treatment' has an endogenous factor ('mediator1'). `glance()` and `summary()` report the chi-square, df and p-value as NA, and `anova()` and `mbco_sem()` refuse. The coefficients equal equation-wise OLS, and the sandwich standard errors (observed information) are unaffected.
decompose(extract_mediation(fit4, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                            outcome = "outcome_int"))
#>        cde    int_ref    int_med        pie        nde        nie      total 
#> 0.04048833 0.07763088 0.22810575 0.32526471 0.11811921 0.55337046 0.67148967 
# }
